medications.dose: 2.5 mg once daily, titrate to 5 mg after 2 weeks, then to 10 mg as tolerated
medications.purpose: Lower clinic blood pressure to <140/90 mmHg (stage 1 hypertension control)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑inhibitor as first‑line monotherapy for non‑Afro‑Caribbean adults aged <55 y (step 1) and advises titration to target BP while monitoring renal function and potassium.

contraindications.reason: ACE‑I are teratogenic and contraindicated in pregnancy (NICE NG136).
contraindications.alternative: If pregnancy is confirmed or possible, use amlodipine 5 mg once daily as first‑line CCB.

contraindications.reason: NICE NG136 contraindicates combined ACE‑I and ARB due to no added benefit and increased renal risk.
contraindications.alternative: Do not add an ARB while on ramipril.

assumptions_warnings: Exact age not provided – assumed <55 y for ACE‑I first‑line; if age ≥55 y, CCB (amlodipine) would be preferred.
Ethnicity not recorded – assumed non‑Afro‑Caribbean; if Afro‑Caribbean, CCB first‑line.
eGFR and serum potassium not available – assumed normal for initiation; baseline renal function and K⁺ must be measured before starting ramipril and repeated 1‑2 weeks after dose changes.
Pregnancy status unknown – must be confirmed before prescribing ramipril.
QRISK cardiovascular risk score not calculated – required to assess need for statin therapy (primary prevention).
Full lipid profile not available – needed for comprehensive CVD risk assessment.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily and titrate to achieve target BP <140/90 mmHg, with monitoring of renal function and potassium. Verify age, ethnicity, eGFR, potassium, and pregnancy status before initiation. Provide lifestyle advice (salt <6 g/day, weight loss, exercise, smoking cessation) and arrange follow‑up BP check in 2 weeks, labs at baseline and 1‑2 weeks, then annual review. If pregnancy is confirmed, switch to amlodipine 5 mg daily.
